_: The Fixer's operator-facing words. Order is the order a person meets them:
the page around the checks, then the checks, then what they find, then the
refusals, the report, and the ways out.
Adding a file here is all it takes to bring its words into the editing file.
Context files are parsed but never extracted from: they are where the
constants and the constructor parameter names live, and without them a key
reads as an argument position instead of as 'what is wrong with mme-in-use'.
title: The words the transmit checks say
blurb: Everything the transmit checks put in front of an operator, pulled out of the code so it can be edited as writing. Change the words; the code keeps working.

files.about: The heading, the state-of-play sentence, the how-to bullets, the buttons and the words for each state a check can be in. This is the frame every check sits inside.
Each check's name, the question it asks, what it does, what pressing Run will do, and the two questions asked before anything transmits.

files.section: What the audio setup check finds
files.about: Stage 0's answer, and everything it can find wrong, with what to do about each one.

files.section: What the microphone and transmit checks find
files.about: Stages 1 to 4: the answer each one gives, and everything they can find wrong.

files.section: When the tool refuses to transmit
files.about: Every reason nothing was sent. These are heard at the moment an operator expected the radio to key, so they have to say what happened and what to do next.
The document the run becomes — the one that goes to a radio manufacturer.

files.section: What the window says while you work
files.about: Announcements, notices and the words for things that happen outside the page itself.
What you are asked on the way out, and what each answer costs.
The window that lists runs already made, and lets one be read again or carried on.
